subject: health
title: Explicit model: handwashing and how germs spread
essentialQuestion: How do everyday routines keep my body well and stop germs from spreading?
materials: index cards or paper for a routine card
soap and water for a handwashing demonstration
keyPoints: Germs are far too small to see, and hands look clean even when they carry them.
Germs move by touch, by coughs and sneezes, and by shared surfaces like door handles and tablets.
Wash with soap and water for about 20 seconds: palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs, and under nails.
Always wash before eating or helping with food, and after the toilet, blowing your nose, touching animals, or coming inside.
Cough and sneeze into your elbow, not your hand, so your hands stay clean for touching things.
privacySafeScenario: Mia pets a neighbour's dog on the walk home, then goes straight to the snack cupboard. What should she do first, and what could happen if she skips it?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about handwashing and how germs spread to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: State the most important rule or fact about handwashing and how germs spread in your own words.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about handwashing and how germs spread.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Any routine step may be described, drawn, sequenced with picture cards, or demonstrated by an adult instead of written. A step a learner cannot do independently is planned as an adult-supported step, which counts fully.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about handwashing and how germs spread under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, choose one routine step from the card to try this week and talk about what made it easier or harder. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
